title: Sort aluminium parts with a GO / NO-GO gap gauge
instruction: Gauge every aluminium block before putting acceptable parts in the green tray and rejects in the red tray. Accept a part only if it enters the GO gap and stays out of the NO-GO gap. Keep unchecked parts out of the finished trays, and leave all parts settled and released. A tipped part can be righted and inspected again.
context: Machinists and inspectors routinely use fixed limit gauges to separate acceptable parts from undersize and oversize stock. An incorrect acceptance can send a defective part downstream. Credit requires a physical gauge reading for each part, including released support, before its disposition.
setup: Station table; metres, x forward, y left, z up; table top 0.7475 m. Three uniform aluminium bars are 90 mm long along x and 40 mm high, cut from common 40 mm thick rectangular stock and machined to width. Block 1: width 25 mm, 243.0 g, starts at xy (0.32,+0.24); block 2: width 30 mm, 291.6 g, at (0.32,-0.24); block 3: width 35 mm, 340.2 g, at (0.32,-0.36). Their bottoms start 1 mm above the table and settle onto it. All are silver and flat, long edges along x. Fixed dark steel gauge base: 120 x 190 x 6 mm, centred at (0.225,0), bottom on the table. Two fixed anvil pairs, each anvil 18 x 24 x 10 mm; their tops are 17 mm above the table and their bottoms 1 mm above the base top, as rigid mounting spacers omitted from collision geometry. GO inner gap 32 mm centred at (0.225,+0.040); NO-GO inner gap 28 mm at (0.225,-0.040). Fixed green tray at (0.145,+0.25), red tray at (0.145,-0.25): each has a 140 x 220 x 3 mm floor; 3 mm thick walls, 10 mm high, with wall bottoms 4 mm above the table. Floors and walls are painted steel. Initial poses and every primitive size are specified in geometry.json; no object jitter. Both the undersize left block and the in-tolerance right block require a transfer between arms at the gauge. All three start and destination locations are fixed.
scoring: Read the end state. Highest tier only: 0 if no inspected part is correctly placed; 0.25 for one; 0.50 for two; 0.75 for all three. A correct placement requires the entire footprint at least 1 mm inside its tray floor, support on that floor, no gripper holding it, and rest. Every part first needs a released, supported GO reading for at least 0.3 s; a GO passer then needs a separate released, supported NO-GO reading for at least 0.3 s. Widths 28 < w < 32 mm are acceptable. A seated reading requires the bottom in contact with the gauge base inside the gap; a blocked reading requires bottom contact patches on both anvil tops with the centre of mass projection at least 1 mm inside their combined support hull. No positive vertical gap is allowed, except 0.5 nanometres of numerical roundoff; up to 0.2 mm solver penetration is tolerated. Tilted or one-sided contact is not a valid reading. Every nearby gripper must have an opening at least the projected gripped width plus 5 mm; unavailable gripper readings give no inspection or placement credit. Rest uses the last 10 position samples, with all pair distances at most 2 mm; before the window fills it uses speed below 10 mm/s and spin below 0.5 rad/s. Gauge readings and final tray placements require tilt at most 0.5 degrees. A tip beyond 15 degrees clears that part's inspection records; righting it and repeating the required inspections can earn credit again. Wrong or unchecked tray placement and leaving x=0.03–0.55 m or abs(y)<=0.57 m are current invalidity gates and clear the affected part's records. Missing or changed geometry, or moving a fixed structure, clears all records. No score is awarded while a current gate is invalid; after repair, repeat the affected inspections. Only a bottom below table height minus 2 mm or speed above 0.8 m/s irreversibly invalidates the episode. Final success, held for 1 s by the framework, alone awards 1.0. In real trials a continuous video establishes release, order and dwell; a photo establishes support by showing no visible gap between the block bottom and the base or anvil tops. A tape or caliper verifies tray margins and dimensions. Held, hovered 0.3 mm above support, or tilted midair poses do not count.
run_limit: 3,000 control steps at 20 Hz (150 seconds). Nominal demo: 2,924 intervals / 146.2 seconds. CPU ideal-settling success hold completes at step 2,826; revised GPU completion is pending.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Return every block to its fixed named start pose, flat, and restore the fixed geometry. A new task process is simplest. In-process history resets only when one block jumps more than 0.10 m in a single step and the entire layout simultaneously returns to nominal; slowly moving parts back cannot erase the below-table or excessive-speed latch. Repairable errors require restoring validity and repeating affected inspections. Start a new overhead video for real trials.
fidelity: Rigid aluminium bars and fixed steel gauge/tray structures use analytic boxes. Gaps are scaled to millimetres, without chamfers, burrs or elastic deformation. Mounting spacers are omitted. Shared framework friction is rubber-like. Support is a conservative geometric contact/COM certificate, not measured contact force. The previous public gripper/TCP reader worked in GPU smoke; new finger-link diagnostics and the revised full physical demo remain GPU-unverified; positive gaps fail closed.
